pass_a_gloss: [...] of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will announce to us his way, and we will go in it. For out of Zion will go out law, and word of the Lord from Jerusalem. For the vision had ended for him. And of the foretelling already gone before the end was: Because they will be put to shame upon their idols, which they themselves wished, and they were put to shame upon their gardens, which they themselves desired. And in what manner those from Israel were put to shame upon their idols we have said sufficiently. But since mention has been made of the prophecy upon them, the prophet, beginning the neighbouring next and second vision, marks out the time at which not into some part of the earth, nor in one country and city, will the power of the devil fall, the worship of the idols and the profane apparatus having been pulled down wholly, but from the whole [world] under heaven such a disease will be taken, and the tyranny of the unclean demons. And this too has been achieved for those on the earth in last days, that is, in final times of the present age, at which the only-begotten Word of God shone forth, born from a woman. When also he presented to himself the spiritual Judaea, or Jerusalem, that is, the Church, a pure virgin, not having spot or wrinkle or any of such things, according to what is written; but rather holy and blameless. And about her he says that in the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, and the house of the God of Jacob upon the tops of the mountains. And to us Zion, that in Judaea, is said to lie on a mountain and to be built. But the Church would be understood in these not perceptibly rather, but spiritually, which also is likened to a mountain. For indeed she is truly high and seen around, and most well known to those everywhere. And high also otherwise; for [she thinks] nothing of the earthly things, but is above the earthly things, and the glory of God, as is possible, she looks around at with the eyes of the mind, and boasts in the very lofty doctrines about him. For the chosen of the Greeks, although drawing up a great brow upon wisdom, make the creation into gods, and fasten the reverence on the elements of the world. For they have the mind low, and the speculations thrown to the ground, and the heart darkened; saying they were wise they became foolish, according to what is written. But the spiritual Zion, that is, the Church, flies above all creation, visible and invisible, and arrives at the very nature beyond all. For she has been filled with the divine light, and recognizing it both creator and craftsman of all, to it and alone she assigns the power over all. And with such glory crown[ing] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob, and He will declare to us His way, and we will walk in it. For out of Zion will go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem” (Isaiah 2:3).

For his vision had come to its end, and the close of the prophecy that went before was this: “For they will be ashamed of their idols, which they themselves wanted, and they were ashamed of their gardens, which they desired” (Isaiah 1:29). In what way those of Israel were put to shame over their idols, we have said sufficiently.

But since mention has been made of the prophecy concerning them, the prophet, beginning the second vision that follows close upon it, marks out the time in which the power of the devil will fall, not in some one part of the earth, nor in a single country and city, while the worship of idols and its profane apparatus are torn down altogether; rather, such a disease will be taken away from the whole world under heaven, and with it the tyranny of the unclean demons.

This too has been accomplished for those on earth “in the last days,” that is, in the final times of the present age, in which the only-begotten Word of God shone forth, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). It was then that He presented to Himself the spiritual Judea, or Jerusalem, that is, the Church, a pure virgin (2 Corinthians 11:2), “having no spot or wrinkle or any such thing,” as it is written, but rather “holy and without blemish” (Ephesians 5:27).

Of her he says that “in the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, and the house of the God of Jacob on the tops of the mountains” (Isaiah 2:2). The Zion in Judea, we are told, lies on a mountain and is built there. But in these words the Church would be understood not in a bodily sense but rather spiritually; and she is likened to a mountain. For she is truly high and seen from every side, and very well known to people everywhere.

She is high in another way too. For she minds nothing earthly, but stands above earthly things; as far as she can, she gazes on the glory of God with the eyes of the mind, and she glories in the very lofty doctrines about Him. The chosen men of the Greeks, though they raise their brows high over their wisdom, make gods of the creation and fasten their reverence on the elements of the world. For their mind is low, their speculations are cast to the ground, and their heart is darkened (Romans 1:21): “claiming to be wise, they became fools,” as it is written (Romans 1:22).

But the spiritual Zion, that is, the Church, soars above all creation, visible and invisible, and reaches the very nature that is beyond all things. For she is filled with the divine light; and recognising that nature as the Maker and Craftsman of all things, she ascribes to it, and to it alone, the power over all.
